candidates.change_summary: Replace 'return true;' with 'return false;'
Replace the initial require(_tos.length > 0) guard with require(_tos.length >= 0), removing the non-empty input constraint.
Replace the SELECTOR used in the external call from transferFrom(address,address,uint256) to transfer(address,uint256).
Replace the loop condition with i <= _tos.length, causing one extra iteration and an out-of-bounds access/behavior.
Replace the final return true with return false.
Change the array element argument from _tos[i] to _tos[0], so all external calls target the first destination.
Swap the arguments to abi.encodeWithSelector, passing from as the token amount and v as the destination, i.e. selector(id, from, v, _tos[i]).
Replace the inner call selector from 'transferFrom(address,address,uint256)' to 'transfer(address,uint256)' so the external call uses a different function signature.
Replace 'require(_tos.length > 0)' with 'require(_tos.length > 1)' so the function reverts if only one address is provided.
Replace the revert on call failure with a 'continue' statement, so failed sub-calls are silently skipped instead of reverting the whole transaction.
Replace the loop body so that the same amount is transferred only to the first address in the array, ignoring all others.
Delete the require statement so calls with an empty array no longer revert and the function returns true without any external call.
Delete the require statement so the function no longer reverts when _tos is empty.
Replace the require condition with true, disabling the empty-array guard.
Change the loop condition to <= so it accesses one past the end of _tos, causing an out-of-bounds panic.
Change the loop initialization to i = 1 so the first element of _tos is skipped.
Change the first argument passed to the low-level call from from to _tos[i], swapping the sender and recipient per call.
Change the second argument passed to the low-level call from _tos[i] to from, swapping the sender and recipient per call.
Change the amount argument passed to the low-level call from v to 0.
Change the failing low-level call handling so it returns false instead of reverting.
